# Publishing

Read these rules before you change what a payload ships, bump a version, or publish. This page holds the full text of the live rules of the group, from [README.md](../README.md).

## NR-36: Central versions live in versions.json `[GAP]`

> `versions.json` is the only authority for a published payload's version.

Old number: 4.3.2.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli version check`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: Set a mirror-only published payload's central and derived package version to 1.0.0-01. The version parser and JSON schema both accept the numeric prerelease identifier with a leading zero; isCanonicalVersion returned true in memory. Using a mirror-only payload avoids relying on npm pack's separate version validation, since published-files skips that payload. Fix: issue I-91.

Issues: I-07, I-91.

Exactly one entry per
`kind: published` manifest package, keyed by its manifest key (names are not unique: two generations share
`@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext`), listed in manifest order, every value canonical SemVer (`x.y.z` or `x.y.z-pre`).
`fhevm-npm version check` enforces coverage both ways, the value shape and the
order; it runs in `check-pre`. A missing entry is never inferred from a package's `package.json`,
because that would let derived state become authoritative — it is added by hand, once.

```jsonc
// ✅ versions.json: the manifest's published payloads, in the manifest's order.
{ "schemaVersion": 1, "packages": { "./host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg": "<N>.0", "./hardhat/v3/plugin/pkg": "<N>.0" } }

// ❌ A range, and a payload the manifest does not publish.
{ "packages": { "./hardhat/v3/plugin/pkg": "^<N>.0", "./hardhat/v3/e2e": "0.0.0" } }
```

## NR-37: Derived versions equal the central version `[GAP]`

> Every derived version equals the central one.

Old number: 4.3.3.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli version check`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: Delete the `version` field of the member's entry (for example `plugin/pkg` in hardhat/v3/package-lock.json): memberEntries() at version-check.ts:234 keeps only entries with `version !== undefined`, so the entry is skipped and `version check` passes; the `?? 'no version'` branch at :96 is unreachable. Low severity: npm writes the field itself. A missing root lockfile is also skipped (:207), but 6.1.1 reports that. Fix: issue I-92.

Issues: I-01, I-07, I-92.

A payload's `package.json` version; in every
installation root whose lockfile records the member — its own root, and any root that links it cross-root — the
`version` npm wrote for it; the version a committed generated file embeds, such as
`foundry/forge-fhevm-std/pkg/src/StdFhevmVersion.sol`; and the version each isolated consumer
fixture's lockfile pins the payload at ([NR-66](../entries/NR-66.md)). The remedy is `fhevm-npm version apply`:
edit `versions.json`, preview with `--dry-run`, apply. It accepts a clean worktree or exactly one unstaged change, that
file; a central version only moves forward; `--allow-downgrade` waives that test whenever it is passed. It is meant for
an old version nothing was ever published under, which the flag does not check: `--check-npmjs` asks the registry only
whether the new version is already there. No dependency spec changes, because member edges are `file:` links ([NR-15](../entries/NR-15.md)).
When a generated file no longer embeds a version, or a consumer lockfile records none, `version apply` cannot rewrite
it, and the check names the generator or the lockfile regeneration to run instead. `npm version` is not a supported path
— it writes derived state first and `version check` fails on it.

```sh
# ✅ The whole workflow. `version apply` writes every derived place; none is edited by hand.
$EDITOR versions.json && make version-plan && make version-apply && git add -A . && git commit

# ❌ Writes package.json first, so the authority is now the one out of date.
npm --prefix hardhat/v3/plugin/pkg version patch
```

## NR-38: Rendered ranges stop at the generation `[GAP]`

> A rendered dependency range is `~<version>`: the target's central version, up to the end of its generation.

Old number: 4.3.4.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli publish check`

Evidence:

- Gap, wrong check: Two installation roots contain same-named published payloads at 1.0.1 and 2.0.1. A plugin links the second directory and correctly renders ~2.0.1. validateRenderedRanges chooses the first same-named member and rejects it in favor of ~1.0.1. Reproduced; names are not globally unique. Fix: issue I-93.

Issues: I-01, I-93, I-123.

A generation is `major.minor` at every version, so a rendered range is a tilde on the target's central version. A
payload built against contracts `<N>.4` renders `~<N>.4`: at least the version it was built and tested against, up to
the next generation, which the tilde excludes. A tilde stops at the end of the generation both below 1.0
(`~0.14.4` stops before `0.15.0`) and from 1.0 on (`~1.0.4` stops before `1.1.0`). A caret does not: below 1.0 it
accepts the same versions as the tilde, but from 1.0 on `^1.0.4` accepts `1.1.0`, the next generation.

The floor is never lower than the version the payload was built against: a lower one lets a consumer who upgrades the
payload keep, from their lockfile, an older dependency that may lack a fix the payload relies on. A contracts patch
still never forces a payload release; the payload raises its floor on its next release. A prerelease central version
renders exactly, since a tilde range does not match prereleases. This is the one range policy; there is no per-edge
configuration.

The floor makes the publish order binding: `publish check --check-npmjs` requires a published version that satisfies
the range, so the target's version must be on npmjs.com before the payload that renders it.

```jsonc
// ✅ In the v3 plugin's tarball, rendered from the file: link by `publish pack` (target central <N>.4).
"@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext": "~<N>.4"

// ❌ A caret: from 1.0 on, ^<N>.4 accepts the next generation.
"@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext": "^<N>.4"

// ❌ The generation floor: a consumer upgrading the plugin can keep contracts <N>.0-<N>.3 and miss a fix.
"@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext": "~<N>.0"

// ❌ Exact: every contracts patch would force a plugin release, or leave consumers with two copies.
"@fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext": "<N>.4"
```

> **Changed.** Until issue I-123, the renderer wrote a caret below 1.0 and a tilde from 1.0 on. Below 1.0 both accept the same versions, so no published range changes its meaning.

## NR-41: A payload never imports a dev package `[GAP]`

> Nothing under `pkg/` imports a `…-dev` package.

Old number: 5.1.2.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Gap, no check: no check scans the source files under a published `pkg/` for a `…-dev` specifier; only its Prettier and ESLint configs are scanned (`fhevm-npm/base/checks/scripts.ts:657-676`). Fix: add the scan.

Issues: I-60.

That import ships a specifier no consumer can resolve. This
is the one guarantee a tarball install used to hold alone, and [NR-40](../entries/NR-40.md) is what makes it a grep.

## NR-47: Dev owners define check:publint and check `[GAP]`

> Every dev owner of an npm-distributed payload defines `check:publint` and the `check` verb wrapping its deliverable validations.

Old number: 5.2.1.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check scripts`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: `"check:publint": "publint ./pkg"` (the rule's own second ❌ example), `"check:publint": "echo ok"`, or dropping `&& attw --pack ./pkg` on a payload that ships types: `check scripts` passes. Fix: issue I-101.

Issues: I-101.

`check:publint` runs `publint --strict` against `pkg/`, and `attw --pack` against it too when
the payload ships type declarations; a Solidity-only payload ships none and runs `publint` alone. Every `check:*` leaf
must be reachable from `check`, except `check:mirror` (network-bound) and generator `--check` conveniences.

`attw --pack` resolves the packed types under node10, node16-cjs, node16-esm and bundler, and by default fails on a
problem in any of them. Under `--profile esm-only`, which an ESM-only payload passes, problems specific to node10 and
node16-cjs do not fail the gate; problems in node16-esm and bundler, and problems not tied to a resolution mode, still
can. Packing stays verified with no `.tgz`. The manifest gate follows `publishedRelPath` and requires these scripts, by
name, on the owning dev package; mirror-only payloads are exempt.

```jsonc
// ✅ --strict fails on warnings, and attw packs the package to resolve its types for real.
"check:publint": "publint --strict ./pkg && attw --pack ./pkg"

// ✅ An ESM-only payload: the same gate, under the profile that matches what it ships.
"check:publint": "publint --strict ./pkg && attw --pack ./pkg --profile esm-only"

// ✅ A Solidity-only payload: no types for attw to resolve.
"check:publint": "publint --strict ./pkg"

// ❌ The required script entry is absent, so no uniform gate can discover the check.
"publint": "publint --strict ./pkg && attw --pack ./pkg"

// ❌ Warnings pass silently, and a payload that ships types never has them resolved, so a broken `exports` can ship.
"check:publint": "publint ./pkg"
```

## NR-48: Exports are the whole public surface `[GAP]`

> A payload with a public API declares `exports`; it is the whole public surface, and stays minimal.

Old number: 5.2.2.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Gap, no check: no check reads `exports`. The package schema makes it optional (`fhevm-npm/base/npm.ts:29`), and `test-consumer` falls back to `main` when it is absent (`fhevm-npm/base/test-consumer.ts:1253-1256`). Fix: check that a published payload with a public API declares `exports`, and that a consumer declares none (issue I-65). Minimality stays guidance.

Issues: I-02, I-65.

What it omits is unreachable, provided the consumer resolves in a mode that honors it. A consumer, such as a
template, imports payloads and is imported by nothing: it has no public API and declares no `exports`.

```text
✅ a plugin: "exports": { ".": …, "./package.json": "./package.json" }
✅ a template: no "exports"
❌ a plugin with no "exports": every file it ships can be imported, so every refactor can break a consumer
```

## NR-52: Every payload file ships or is excluded `[GAP]`

> Every file in an npm-distributed payload directory is published or deliberately excluded.

Old number: 5.2.6.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check published-files`

Evidence:

- Gap, wrong check: Add a correctly whitelisted and packed src/café.ts. With Git's default core.quotePath, gitVisibleFiles returns a C-quoted escaped spelling, while npm returns the real UTF-8 path. The packed-set lookup reports the compliant file as stray. Newline/tab filenames similarly break the line-based reader. Fix: issue I-105.

Issues: I-105.

`files` is a
whitelist, so a file that sits beside it without being selected is dead weight: committed under `pkg/`, shipped to
nobody, reviewed by nobody. The check takes the repository-visible files of the payload directory (tracked and
untracked-unignored, as [NR-70](../entries/NR-70.md) discovers), asks npm what it would pack (`npm pack --dry-run`, scripts skipped), and
requires each file to be either in that tarball or matched by a `!` pattern in `files`. The `!` pattern is the one
place a deliberately unpublished file is declared; npm reads a pattern without a `/` at any depth, and so does the
check. A published package without `files` fails outright, since without the whitelist every stray file ships.
Mirror-only payloads are exempt: their directory is the mirror, and its unpublished files are the point.

```jsonc
// ✅ The tsconfig beside the sources is declared unpublished, so it may stay.
"files": ["src", "_types", "LICENSE", "README.md", "!**/tsconfig*.json", "!**/*.tsbuildinfo"]
```

```text
❌ pkg/NOTES.md      present, not selected by "files", named by no "!" pattern: delete it or declare it
❌ pkg/tsconfig.json present, "files": ["src", "_types"] says nothing about it
❌ no "files" at all in a published package.json
```

## NR-53: Ship the license and the front page `[GAP]`

> Every published package carries the repository license, and every npm-distributed payload also carries its front page.

Old number: 5.2.7.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check package-json`

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: In the mirror-only payload hardhat/v2/fhevm-hardhat-template/pkg, replace LICENSE by a symlink to ../../../../LICENSE: existingFile() uses statSync, which follows the link, so the 'regular file' test passes, and published-files.ts skips mirror-only payloads; the mirror then receives a dangling link. On a case-insensitive disk a file named `license` also passes there, but the Linux CI catches that one. Narrow: an npm-distributed payload is safe because npm does not pack a symlink and 5.2.6 then reports it. Fix: issue I-106.

Issues: I-07, I-106.

- Every published package sets `"license": "BSD-3-Clause-Clear"` exactly in its `package.json`, and a regular
  file named exactly `LICENSE` sits beside that `package.json`. The field supports registry metadata; the file
  ensures the payload carries the license text.
- An npm-distributed payload also has `README.md` in the payload directory, and names both `LICENSE` and
  `README.md` in `files`. They are the two files npmjs.com renders on a package page: the license text and the
  front page. npm packs both whatever `files` says, so the listing exists for the reader, not for npm: a whitelist
  that omits them reads as if the package shipped without them.
- Names are exact: `LICENSE` and `README.md`, not `license` or `readme`.

```jsonc
// ✅ The whitelist is the complete manifest of what ships.
"files": ["src", "_types", "LICENSE", "README.md", "!**/tsconfig*.json"]

// ❌ Both files sit in pkg/ and npm packs them, yet the list says otherwise.
"files": ["src", "_types", "!**/tsconfig*.json"]
```

## NR-55: One dev owner per published package `[HOLD]`

> Every published package has exactly one dev owner carrying its applicable conventional checks.

Old number: 5.3.2.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli check ownership`

The validator
resolves each dev entry's `publishedRelPath`, checks the inverse (every published entry has exactly one dev owner),
and applies [NR-47](../entries/NR-47.md) (`check`, `check:publint`) and [NR-54](../entries/NR-54.md) (`test:consumer`) to owners of npm-distributed payloads only.

```jsonc
// ✅ In npm-manifest.json, the dev entry identifies the published payload it owns.
{
  "./hardhat/v2/plugin": {
    "kind": "dev",
    "publishedRelPath": "./hardhat/v2/plugin/pkg",
  },
}
```

```jsonc
// ✅ In hardhat/v2/plugin/package.json, the owning dev package exposes the conventional checks.
"scripts": {
  "check": "npm run check:publint && npm run check:vendored-origin",
  "check:publint": "publint --strict ./pkg && attw --pack ./pkg",
  "test:consumer": "node ../../../fhevm-npm/fhevm-npm.ts test-consumer ./hardhat/v2/fhevm-hardhat-template/pkg --run --build-linked-dependencies"
}

// ❌ Package-specific names are not the conventional entry points the validator requires.
"scripts": {
  "check:package": "publint --strict ./pkg",
  "test:hardhat-template": "node ../../../fhevm-npm/fhevm-npm.ts test-consumer ./hardhat/v2/fhevm-hardhat-template/pkg --run --build-linked-dependencies"
}
```

## NR-61: Packaging linters supplement consumer tests `[GAP]`

> Packaging linters supplement the consumer test.

Old number: 5.3.8.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- Gap, no check: `"compile": "npm run pack:tarball && tsc -p ."` on a dev owner, or `$(call run,...,pack:tarball)` as a prerequisite of a compile target in the Makefile: every check passes. Fix: issue I-111.

Issues: I-111.

The `check:publint` gate of [NR-47](../entries/NR-47.md) remains mandatory:
`publint --strict` for metadata, and `attw --pack` for type resolution where the payload ships types. Neither replaces
runtime execution of the isolated installed payload. `pack:tarball` remains a release-artifact command, never a
prerequisite of the daily workspace loop.

```jsonc
// ✅ Static packaging checks and the installed-artifact test cover different failures.
"scripts": {
  "check:publint": "publint --strict ./pkg && attw --pack ./pkg",
  "test:consumer": "node ../../../fhevm-npm/fhevm-npm.ts test-consumer ./hardhat/v2/fhevm-hardhat-template/pkg --run"
}

// ❌ Type-resolution analysis alone does not execute the installed runtime artifact.
"scripts": { "check:publint": "publint --strict ./pkg && attw --pack ./pkg" }
```

## NR-63: A tarball carries only registry specs `[GAP]`

> A tarball for an npm-distributed payload carries only registry specs and the central version.

Old number: 5.3.10.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli publish check`

Evidence:

- Gap, wrong check: The same-named payloads in separate roots counterexample from NR-38 makes a correct ~2.0.1 tarball fail against the first member's ~1.0.1. Fix: issue I-112.

Issues: I-48, I-112.

`file:` links
are right in the tree ([NR-15](../entries/NR-15.md)) and wrong on npmjs.com, which cannot resolve a path; `fhevm-npm publish pack` is the only
producer of a tarball, and it renders every link per [NR-38](../entries/NR-38.md) into a staged copy before `npm pack`, so the tree is never
touched. `fhevm-npm publish check <payload>` reads the tarball with `tar` and fails on any surviving `file:` spec, a
version other than the central one, a dependency on another payload whose range is not what that payload's
central version renders to, or an entry point the shipped `package.json` declares (`main`, `module`,
`types`, `bin`, any `exports` leaf) that the tarball does not contain — `files` is a whitelist, so a built
entry point left out of it publishes a package that resolves to nothing, and the `publint`/`attw` gate of
[NR-61](../entries/NR-61.md) inspects the payload directory rather than this artifact. With `--check-npmjs` it also requires every rendered range to
have a published satisfying version — retried, because the previous release job publishes the dependency moments earlier
— and the payload's own version to be absent, never retried. `fhevm-npm publish order` derives a sequence from the
links. The release workflow writes a dependency order down by hand, as one job per payload, each waiting for the one
before; nothing checks it against `publish order`. In a real release the order is still enforced by refusal, since each
job's `publish check --check-npmjs` refuses a payload whose dependency is not on npmjs.com yet. Before the first job,
`fhevm-npm publish rehearse` packs every payload of the release set into the tarballs directory and checks them
together, in publish order, a dependency inside the set being satisfied by its freshly packed tarball, so a payload a
later job would refuse stops the release before anything is published; `make publish-rehearse` runs the same rehearsal
on a developer machine. `publish render <payload>` shows the same rendering without producing anything.

```sh
# ✅ Before any job publishes: the whole release set packed and checked together.
# The excluded payload key is illustrative.
fhevm-npm publish rehearse --exclude "./example-owner/pkg"

# ✅ Then one job per payload $p, in the workflow's dependency order, each payload proven just before it goes out.
tgz=$(fhevm-npm publish pack "$p")
fhevm-npm publish render "$p"
fhevm-npm publish check "$p" --check-npmjs
npm publish "$tgz"

# ❌ Publishes the working tree: the tarball ships "file:../../../../host-contracts-cleartext/<vN>/pkg".
npm publish ./hardhat/v3/plugin/pkg
```

## NR-88: The Hardhat 2 plugin's version constants follow their sources `[HOLD]`

> The two package versions that the Hardhat 2 plugin writes in `src/internal/constants.ts` equal their sources of truth.

Check: script.

Checked by: `./fhevm-npm-cli sync hh-v2-constants --check`

The Hardhat 2 plugin, `hardhat/v2/plugin/pkg`, hardcodes two package versions in `src/internal/constants.ts` and reads
them at run time:

- `FHEVM_HOST_CONTRACTS_CLEARTEXT_PACKAGE` equals the version that `versions.json` gives the host-contracts-cleartext
  payload, at the key the plugin's own `file:` dependency points to. The rule follows the plugin when it moves to
  another generation.
- `FHEVM_SOLIDITY_PACKAGE` equals the floor of the `@fhevm/solidity` spec in `npm-manifest.json#dependencies.pinned`:
  `^X.Y.Z` gives `X.Y.Z`, the release whose addresses the block was checked against.

Each block carries its version twice, in the comment above it and in its `version` field. Both equal the source.

`version apply` writes the derived versions of [NR-37](../entries/NR-37.md) and `sync pinned` writes the pins of
[NR-21](../entries/NR-21.md), but neither touches this file. Without this rule it drifts silently after a version bump or a pin
change, and the plugin then describes a package that the workspace no longer builds. The remedy is
`fhevm-npm sync hh-v2-constants`, which rewrites only those four spots. `--check` compares instead of writing, and runs
in `make check-pre`.

The rule applies to Hardhat 2 only. When `hardhat/v2` is deleted, retire this rule together with the command: the
header of `fhevm-npm/commands/sync-hh-v2-constants.ts` lists what goes.

```ts
// ✅ Both spots equal the source: versions.json gives the payload X.Y.Z.
// @fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext@X.Y.Z
FHEVM_HOST_CONTRACTS_CLEARTEXT_PACKAGE: {
  version: 'X.Y.Z',

// ❌ The version moved in versions.json, and the constant still names the old release.
// @fhevm/host-contracts-cleartext@X.Y.W
```
